nodes.label: Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Remember that maybe a tenth of what's remarkable at Stanford lives at the GSB - a starter set of the rest, all a few minutes bike ride from where you sleep
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: The Dish: a 3.7-mile loop through the foothills past a 150-foot radio telescope built in 1961 - a Cold-War instrument that later talked to the Voyager spacecraft and still operates; sunrise or sunset is the move, no bikes on the loop; the signature Stanford side quest (dish.stanford.edu)
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: The Cantor Arts Center is free and holds one of the largest collections of Rodin bronzes outside Paris, including a cast of The Gates of Hell; the outdoor sculpture garden is open 24/7 (museum.stanford.edu)
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Next door, the Anderson Collection (also free; Thursday-Monday 11-5, no reservation) is a jaw-dropping room of postwar American art - Rothko, de Kooning, and Pollock's Lucifer
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: The Papua New Guinea Sculpture Garden: a true deep cut, sixty-plus works carved on-site in 1994 by master carvers brought from the Sepik River; free tours run the fourth Sunday of each month
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Nearby, the 1880s Arizona Cactus Garden is a quiet, photogenic place to reset
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Hoover Tower's 250-foot observation deck (free for Stanford affiliates; bring binoculars) sees San Francisco on a clear day
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Windhover is a free contemplative center built around Nathan Oliveira's paintings, with an outdoor labyrinth - the campus's best-kept quiet spot
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Big science you can actually visit: SLAC, the two-mile linear accelerator (the longest in the world until 2017, and the source of six Nobel Prizes), runs free ninety-minute public tours a couple of times a month - register ahead
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: The Coffee House ('the CoHo') has been the student living room since 1966 - coffee, beer, open mics
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Memorial Church and the sandstone Main Quad are the architectural heart of campus
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Tradition to catch: Full Moon on the Quad (October)
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Tradition to catch: fountain hopping - there's an unofficial ranking, and President Levin admits he did it
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Tradition to catch: Primal Scream (midnight screaming during dead week)
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Tradition to catch: the Leland Stanford Junior University Marching Band (LSJUMB) - the 'band' that scatters instead of marching and has been fined by the NCAA and banned from Disneyland (Stanford magazine)
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Make something with your hands: the Product Realization Lab (PRL) is a hands-on fabrication and manufacturing shop open to students through its courses
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: ME 203, Design and Fabrication, teaches you to actually run the mill, the lathe, and the rest of real on-the-ground manufacturing
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: making.stanford.edu indexes every campus shop and studio - welding, woodworking, laser-cutting, 3D printing - most with open hours and quarter-long classes
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: The LOFT is a graduate design studio worth getting a friend to walk you into
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: The Stanford educational farm: for the opposite of a machine shop, classes in regenerative agriculture where an afternoon's 'work' is harvesting snap peas - sometimes literally touching grass is the whole point
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: CCRMA (say 'karma'), the Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics, up at The Knoll, is where music meets code - synthesis, spatial audio, and the Stanford Laptop Orchestra (SLOrk); runs a concert series of new computer music, join the mailing list; open courses like Music 101
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: The Stanford Bookstore: the official four-floor campus store, with the Cardinal Technology Center - Stanford apparel and gifts on the main floor, faculty-authored books and a cafe upstairs, textbooks and supplies in the basement, computers and software (often at education pricing) at the tech center
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Stanford Live: the university's professional performing-arts presenter, at Bing Concert Hall and the open-air Frost Amphitheater; students get deeply discounted tickets (usually two per show with your ID), free masterclasses, and artist talks
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Continuing Studies: open-enrollment evening and online courses - liberal arts, creative writing, wellness, professional skills - that anyone can take with no application; a low-key way for you, a partner, or family to take a Stanford class purely for the joy of it
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Field stations, if you wander: Jasper Ridge Biological Preserve, 1,200 acres of protected foothills open by docent-led tour
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Field stations, if you wander: Hopkins Marine Station, Stanford's 1892 marine lab next door to the Monterey Bay Aquarium
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: The Stanford Theatre: off campus but essential - a lovingly restored 1925 movie palace on University Avenue (funded by the Packard family) that screens Hollywood classics from 1910-1970 on 35mm, with a live Wurlitzer organ between shows; a perfect low-cost date night
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: The McMurtry Building: the home of Art & Art History, right beside the Cantor and the Anderson - a striking Diller Scofidio + Renfro building (2015) with art studios, film and media labs, the Bowes Art & Architecture Library, and ground-floor galleries and a roof garden open to visitors
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: The Red Barn: Stanford's historic horse barn, out toward the foothills, home to the Stanford Riding Academy - English and western riding lessons open to students, staff, and community on a quarterly schedule (there's even a for-credit wellness version)
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Bing Nursery School: Stanford's laboratory preschool in the southeast corner of campus, which doubles as a child-development research site (the famous 'marshmallow test' ran here); play-based, half-day sessions from age two to kindergarten, competitive to get into so ask early
nodes.source_location: Chapter 8: Getting Oriented - Deep cuts: the Stanford side quests

nodes.label: Frost, in festival mode: beyond the professional Stanford Live shows, the amphitheater hosts two beloved student-run festivals - the end-of-year Frost Music & Arts Festival (run by the student Stanford Concert Network) and Blackfest, a celebration of Black art and community - both with real touring headliners

nodes.source_location: Chapter 11 - The AI accounts Stanford gives you

nodes.label: As of June 30, 2026, Stanford has an enterprise education agreement with OpenAI, and every active student gets an account - ignore old workarounds about bolting a personal ChatGPT account onto your Stanford email. It is part of a campus AI pilot running through August 2027, so assume the details will move (Stanford UIT's ChatGPT Edu page)
nodes.source_location: Chapter 11 - The AI accounts Stanford gives you

nodes.label: Use it with eyes open: your chat history and personal context live on an account tied to your Stanford identity, and historically migrating an account's history out when you graduate has been painful to impossible. Keep long-running projects and anything you'd hate to lose on a personal account, and treat the Stanford-provided AI as at-your-own-risk convenience
nodes.source_location: Chapter 11 - The AI accounts Stanford gives you

nodes.label: ChatGPT Edu (Standard) - free with an active SUNet ID. You get higher message limits than the free tier, data analysis, web browsing, document summarization, Codex for coding help, and the ability to build custom GPTs. Request it through the UIT service page. There is also a Pro tier, but it needs a funding source (a PTA)
nodes.source_location: Chapter 11 - The AI accounts Stanford gives you

nodes.label: Claude for Education and Gemini Enterprise - Stanford runs the same arrangement with Anthropic and Google, so you can pick the model you actually like rather than paying for three subscriptions

nodes.label: The AI Playground - Stanford's own sandbox for trying models side by side, with an AI API gateway if you're building something
nodes.source_location: Chapter 11 - The AI accounts Stanford gives you

nodes.label: Why to use the Stanford account: ChatGPT Edu is approved for low-, moderate-, and high-risk data (including PHI), your conversations aren't used to train OpenAI's models, and it carries extra copyright protections. nodes.label: Flights home: the 6 a.m. straight-from-the-party flight and the 2–3 p.m. brunch-first flight both have fans; around 12:30 p.m. threads the needle (checkout at 11, ten minutes to the airport, some sleep first); the worst window is 8–10 a.m. — parties end at 3–4 a.m. and you'll sit in the airport, tired and miserable
nodes.source_location: Social Life — Vegas FOAM, Tactically

nodes.label: Classmates have rented club tables at Omnia for afterparties, taken over a Taco Bell Cantina for a chaotic pregame, and hosted birthday pregames in a Bellagio penthouse — the generosity of the class makes the weekend; budget accordingly and say yes
nodes.source_location: Social Life — Vegas FOAM, Tactically

nodes.label: WAAAM — the cross-school Asian-MBA Vegas weekend, typically the first weekend of spring quarter, draws four-hundred-plus MBAs from Asian business-student associations across the top programs, with headliner DJs in recent years; tickets close about a month out; GSB signups run through ABSA
nodes.source_location: Social Life — Vegas FOAM, Tactically

nodes.label: Executive Challenge — a full-day fall MBA1 event (calendared 7:30 a.m.–7:30 p.m., usually done by ~4:30) with MBA2 coaches and real executives judging; attendance is strictly enforced
nodes.source_location: Social Life — Traditions You'll Want Context For

nodes.label: Shenanigans — an old MBA tradition: sections compete all quarter to perform small, pre-planned, harmless disruptions in class; points are logged in a shared doc and posted to #shenanigans; the winning section gets a prize on par with Executive Challenge's; professors mostly play along
nodes.source_location: Social Life — Traditions You'll Want Context For

nodes.label: Shenanigans examples from the class of '26 tracker: wear a t-shirt with a sectionmate's face on it and sit next to them; pop non-alcoholic champagne in class (bonus for pouring a glass); start the wave in your row; arrive late on rollerblades and blade to your seat
nodes.source_location: Social Life — Traditions You'll Want Context For

nodes.label: GSB Show — the annual student sketch/musical comedy production
nodes.source_location: Social Life — Traditions You'll Want Context For

nodes.label: Comedy Night (the stand-up night) — a real stage for classmates' sets, in the warmest room you'll ever play
nodes.source_location: Social Life — Traditions You'll Want Context For

nodes.label: LOWKeynotes — the TED-style student speaker series: "if those give you a stage, TALK gives you a heart"
nodes.source_location: Social Life — Traditions You'll Want Context For

nodes.label: Window Wars — once a year, first-floor residence students cook food in their dorm rooms and "sell" it out their windows
nodes.source_location: Social Life — Traditions You'll Want Context For

nodes.label: Big Game — Stanford vs. Cal, the Saturday at the start of Thanksgiving break, alternating campuses: "go at least once"
